title: After Twenty Years
author: O. Henry
summary: At about ten on a cold, windy, rain-threatening night in New York, a policeman on his beat walks up a nearly empty avenue, trying doors and twirling his club. In the doorway of a darkened hardware store he finds a man with an unlit cigar.

The man explains that twenty years ago this was 'Big Joe' Brady's restaurant. Here he dined with his best chum, Jimmy Wells, the night before he left for the West to make his fortune. They promised to meet at this spot exactly twenty years later, whatever their conditions. He has done well; he shows off a gold watch set with diamonds and a large diamond scarf-pin, which the policeman sees in the light of a match. He is sure Jimmy, 'the truest, staunchest old chap', will come. The policeman asks how long he will wait and walks on.

Soon a tall man in a long overcoat arrives, calling himself Jimmy Wells. They walk arm in arm. At a brightly lit drug store the man from the West notices that his friend has a pug nose, not Jimmy's Roman nose. The tall man is a plain-clothes policeman. He arrests 'Silky' Bob, a criminal wanted in Chicago, and hands him a note from Jimmy.

The note says that Jimmy was on time at the meeting place. When Bob struck the match, Jimmy recognised the face of the man wanted in Chicago. He could not bring himself to arrest his old friend, so he sent a plain-clothes man to do it.
O. Henry (William Sydney Porter, 1862–1910) is famous for surprise endings; the story appeared in The Four Million (1906). It is told by a third-person omniscient narrator.
Foreshadowing: the appointment made twenty years ago, the face seen in the match-light and the 'Jimmy' who seems taller hint at the ending.
Themes: friendship and loyalty against duty, how time changes people.

Simple sentence (one main clause), compound sentence (two main clauses joined by and, but, or, so …) and complex sentence (a main clause with one or more dependent clauses). One word can have more than one meaning (beat, club, figure, motion …).

sa2: Why was Bob confident that Jimmy would come to meet him?
He believed Jimmy was the truest and staunchest friend in the world, who would keep his word. He felt that if Jimmy was alive, he would surely be there.
What was the promise made by Bob and Jimmy twenty years ago?

The night before Bob left for the West, they dined at 'Big Joe' Brady's and promised to meet at the same place, at ten o'clock, exactly twenty years later, whatever their condition or however far they had to travel.
Describe the setting of the story.
It is ten o'clock at night on a cold, windy New York avenue with a taste of rain. The streets are almost deserted, and the shops, like the hardware store, are dark.
How had time changed Bob and Jimmy?
Bob had become rich in the West by living on his wits, but he had also turned into a criminal. Jimmy had stayed in New York, become a policeman and remained honest and loyal to his duty.
Why did Bob's hands tremble as he read the note?
He had expected a happy reunion, but the note told him that his friend Jimmy was the policeman who had recognised him and arranged his arrest. The shock made his hands tremble.

He wanted to keep faith with his old friend and his promise, but as a policeman it was his duty to arrest a wanted criminal. He chose duty, but sent another officer because he could not arrest Bob himself.
sa3: What does the note from Jimmy reveal about his character?

It shows that Jimmy kept the appointment loyally, but was an honest policeman who put duty above friendship. It also shows his tenderness: he could not bear to arrest his old friend himself, so he sent a plain-clothes man and explained gently in a note.
Bring out the surprise ending of 'After Twenty Years'.

We expect a happy reunion of two old friends. Instead the 'Jimmy' who arrives is a plain-clothes man who arrests Bob, and we learn that the patrolling policeman was Jimmy himself, who recognised Bob as a wanted criminal in the match-light.

or: Do you like the character of Bob? Give reasons.

Bob is likable for his loyalty — he travels a thousand miles to keep a twenty-year-old promise and speaks warmly of Jimmy. But he is also boastful, showing off his watch and pin, and he has become a criminal. So he wins sympathy but not admiration.

sa3: How does O. Henry create atmosphere in the story?

The cold wind, the drizzle and the nearly empty streets create a gloomy, tense mood. The dark doorway, the match-light on Bob's face and the bright drug-store lights where the truth is revealed build suspense and make the ending striking.
